text:
Rice growth is divided into three phases covering nine numbered growth stages (stage 0 through stage 9).

Vegetative phase: Stage 0 is germination; Stage 1 is the seedling stage; Stage 2 is tillering; Stage 3 is stem elongation. The overall length of the vegetative phase depends on the variety (it is not fixed, unlike the two phases below).

Reproductive phase: Stage 4 is panicle initiation; Stage 5 is booting; Stage 6 is heading (flowering). The reproductive phase lasts approximately 35 days regardless of variety.

Ripening phase: Stage 7 is the milk (watery grain-fill) stage; Stage 8 is the dough stage; Stage 9 is full maturity. The ripening phase lasts approximately 30 days regardless of variety.

So total time from panicle initiation to maturity is about 65 days (35 + 30), on top of a variety-dependent vegetative period.
